title: Day 4 Activity and Assignment
summary: Role-play a supervisor correcting incomplete room preparation, then identify two personal improvement areas and how you will work on them.

items.label: Focus
items.body: Emotional intelligence, receiving correction, sincere apologies and giving feedback without humiliation

sections.title: Activity: Room-preparation correction
paragraphs: A supervisor corrects a staff member for failing to prepare a massage room properly.
Work in groups of three. One person is the supervisor, one is the staff member, and one observes.
Use the same facts in every version: used towels have not been removed, the bed is not ready, and massage oil has not been replenished. The next client is due soon.
First, demonstrate an unconstructive version. Then replay the same situation with a constructive version.
The observer should note what changed. Do not name real colleagues.

sections.title: The situation
paragraphs: The supervisor notices that Room 2 is not ready after a session.
She says: "Please ensure that the used towels are removed, the bed is properly prepared and the supplies are checked before the next appointment."

sections.title: Unconstructive responses to demonstrate
paragraphs: Show how Day 4 problems look in practice. Choose at least two of the following.
list: The staff member becomes angry, raises her voice, or walks away.
The staff member becomes defensive: "Why are you always disturbing me? Am I the only person working here?"
The staff member treats the correction as a personal attack: "You think I'm incompetent."
The staff member conceals the mistake or blames the previous therapist without checking the facts.
The supervisor humiliates the staff member in front of colleagues or a client.
The supervisor uses insults: "You're so careless. You never do anything properly."

sections.title: Constructive version
paragraphs: Replay the same situation using what you learned in Day 4.
list: The supervisor corrects the behaviour, not the person's identity, and speaks privately if practical. Urgent safety or client delays may require immediate, respectful redirection.
The staff member listens, applies FACT, and does not treat firm feedback as an automatic attack.
The staff member admits the part that belongs to her, apologises sincerely, and corrects the room now.
If the facts are incomplete, she asks a clarifying question instead of arguing.
If the supervisor used insults, the staff member still addresses the room problem and requests respectful communication.
Both agree on one practical improvement, such as completing the room checklist before leaving.

sections.title: Observer questions
list: Was the supervisor correcting the room issue or attacking the person?
Did the staff member listen before reacting?
Was the apology specific, or only the word "sorry"?
Was the conversation private enough for the situation?
What would you do differently on a real shift?

sections.title: Optional extra scenes
paragraphs: If time allows, replay one extra scene using CARE when giving feedback and OWN IT when admitting a mistake.

items.label: Scene A — Public embarrassment
items.body: The supervisor announces the incomplete room in front of other staff. Replay with a private, specific correction.

items.label: Scene B — Defensive reaction
items.body: The staff member says: "You're always picking on me." Replay with listening, acknowledging the checklist, and explaining relevant facts without hostility.

sections.title: Assignment: Two areas for improvement
paragraphs: Identify two areas where you need improvement and how you intend to work on them.
Choose areas connected to Day 4: managing emotions, receiving correction, admitting mistakes, apologising sincerely, or giving feedback without embarrassing others.
Be specific. "I will be better" is not enough. Name the habit, when it happens at work, and the practical step you will take.

sections.title: How to complete the assignment
list: Area 1: What do you currently do, and when does it happen at Zura Spa?
Area 1: How does it affect colleagues, clients or the schedule?
Area 1: What will you practise instead, and how will you check that you did it?
Area 2: What do you currently do, and when does it happen at Zura Spa?
Area 2: How does it affect colleagues, clients or the schedule?
Area 2: What will you practise instead, and how will you check that you did it?

sections.title: Examples you may adapt
list: When I am corrected, I interrupt. I will listen to the full point, then ask one clarifying question if needed.
When I make a booking error, I look for someone else to blame. I will check the facts, admit my part, and report it promptly.
When I am frustrated with a colleague, I correct her in front of others. I will speak privately, describe the behaviour, and request a clear next step.
When I feel insulted, I argue immediately. I will pause, apply FACT, and respond to the work issue first.

remember: A room that is not ready is a work issue. Correct it firmly without humiliation. Receive the correction without hostility, admit what is yours, and put the room right. Then name two habits you will improve on the floor.
